So update from $LITE + Win Semi ( $SIVE ) foundry:  

Lumentum in a meeting with Stifel at ECOC 2026 stated:

- $NVDA Spectrum-6 CPO UHP demands increased materially. 
- NPO as larger than CPO, with multi-wavelength external lasers lifting ASPs (Sivers offers multi wave length DFB arrays, read through on higher valued products)
- Demand for UHP lasers continues to exceed supply

- Win has strengthened inventory management for InP substrates while moving toward 6-in InP wafers for ongoing process testing. Currently relies on Tier-1 International suppliers.  
- Many of this was spent on DUV tools from $ASML but (Win Semi's orders spanned machinery, equipment, and fab engineering work)

So that answers a lot of questions about Sivers' partner "how is this company securing InP substrates", "4in vs 6in", "production timing"

TLDR:
- NPO > CPO (per Lite), multi-wavelength lasers going brrr for prices
- demand > supply (continuation)
- Not sure why people have been bear posting Win Semi when turns out they have everything needed to mass produce CW lasers.

The WSJ alleges the dark blue bars are potential evidence of wash trading on the platform due to a uniform size of $5,500

video games industry going through a much needed rationalization

unfortunately, the player base is not growing the way it once was, and there are simply too many games which cost too much money produced every year at this point

big issue now is spiraling hardware costs, which could make things much worse

only hardware manufacturer trying to work coherently around this seems to be Nintendo, with lower spec hardware which is still performant at PS4 level and provides a portable/handheld (read second screen) experience which could maintain traction in a modern environment

meanwhile, Sony and Microsoft seem to be working on even more expensive, higher spec next gen hardware which almost no one will be able to afford (likely $1K or more)

as a higher spec console gamer, i’d like to see that hardware, sure, but the reality is it won’t be good for me if no one else can afford it. further, people have not gotten the potential out of their existing consoles. and PS5 Pro already offers a premium performance tier for those who want it

what i’d like to see is console makers commit another 4-5 years to existing hardware *exclusively* and push it to the limit while simultaneously doing whatever they can to make it even cheaper

if they don’t, i think we could very well see either Xbox or Playstation effectively die in the next gen. i think demand for cloud gaming is also dramatically overstated and simply does not work well for most players globally

maybe an AI bear market would fix things, but tbh i don’t think it will. the consumer is just tapped out
